findings.body:
**Provide access to the runtime evidence.**

In a fresh checkout, neither linked file exists: `state/` is ignored and the files are not tracked. The review link in `REVIEW.md:47` has the same problem. Readers cannot inspect the referenced deployment or review evidence from these documents.

Provide an accessible evidence location or document how to retrieve the host-local records.
findings.title: Provide access to the runtime evidence.

findings.body:
**Keep report writes outside the source checkout.**

Unlike staging and archive paths, `--report` can point inside the checkout. Line 462 writes after the final checkout check and after the lock is released.

For example, `--report <repo>/build-report.json` makes a successful build leave an untracked file that blocks the next build. Selecting `<repo>/pnpm-lock.yaml` overwrites tracked source.

Reject report paths within the checkout before starting the build. Keep external report paths supported.
findings.title: Keep report writes outside the source checkout.

findings.body:
**Finalize the process group before releasing the checkout lock.**

In `build-runner.py`, Line 136, a nonzero exit bypasses `_kill_process_group`. If a build script starts a background writer with redirected streams and then exits 1, `communicate()` can finish while that writer remains active. It does not terminate the process group. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/subprocess.html?utm_source=openai))

The exception then releases `_exclusive_checkout`. A retry can race with the surviving writer and package modified `dist/` files.

Confirm that the process group has exited after normal `communicate()` completion, before returning or raising. Preserve the existing timeout cleanup.
findings.title: Finalize the process group before releasing the checkout lock.

findings.body:
**Reject non-object `package.json` values.**

If a clean pinned checkout contains `[]` in `package.json`, decoding succeeds, but Line 184 raises `AttributeError`. `main()` does not catch that exception. With `--json`, the command emits a traceback instead of one JSON error artifact.

Check `isinstance(package, dict)` before `.get()` and raise `BuildError` if the check fails. Valid package objects retain the current pin checks.

As per coding guidelines, “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty” and errors must produce one JSON artifact.
findings.title: Reject non-object `package.json` values.

findings.body:
**Distinguish declared Node commands from eligible switches.**

The adapter section at Line 107 lists `publish` and `backfill inventory` as declared alongside `watchdog`. The publisher also passes the completion-budget check described at Line 160. Update this overview so operators do not rule out Node publisher switches. Keep the separate warning that the backfill schedule still refuses.
findings.title: Distinguish declared Node commands from eligible switches.

findings.body:
**Require the same guest boot ID across the manager restart.**

If the guest reboots after the restart command succeeds but before the next snapshot, both manager identifiers can change. `build_checks` then credits a manager restart on a stable guest, and `verify` recomputes the same result. Require matching, nonempty before-and-after boot IDs for `manager_restarted`. Keep the separate reboot check for changed boot IDs.
findings.title: Require the same guest boot ID across the manager restart.

findings.body:
**Select the SSH forwarding port at launch, not at prepare time.**

Two `prepare` calls can both save port 2222 because `free_port()` closes its socket. Once the first guest binds 2222, the second guest cannot bind it, and retrying `boot` uses the same saved port. Select the port under the launch lock, retry bind collisions within a fixed budget, and persist the port used by the successful launch.
findings.title: Select the SSH forwarding port at launch, not at prepare time.

findings.body:
**Do not stop a scope that was not present during the ownership check.**

If `process.json` is absent and `systemctl show` reports `not-found`, cleanup still stops the derived scope by name. A second state directory with the same run ID can create that scope between the query and the stop. The two directories hold different locks, so cleanup can stop the second directory's guest. In systemd 255, `show` can return the `not-found` properties successfully. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v255/src/systemctl/systemctl-show.c))

Skip the stop when the scope is absent. Bind new scope names to the resolved run directory, and require positive ownership before stopping an existing scope. Based on learnings, different state directories can share a run-ID-derived scope name under the same manager.
findings.title: Do not stop a scope that was not present during the ownership check.

findings.body:
**Return one JSON error when an operator interrupts `--json` mode.**

If the operator presses Ctrl-C during SSH readiness, the boot command attempts cleanup and re-raises `KeyboardInterrupt`. The CLI does not catch it, so stdout has no JSON error. Handle `KeyboardInterrupt` at the CLI boundary after cleanup and preserve the existing exception notes. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/exceptions.html?utm_source=openai))

As per coding guidelines, “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty,” and stdout remains “exactly one JSON artifact.”
findings.title: Return one JSON error when an operator interrupts `--json` mode.

findings.body:
**Clean up a failed boot before releasing `run.lock`.**

If `boot()` raises before returning a launch identity, both CLI paths release `run.lock` before cleanup. If another invocation boots the same run in that gap, cleanup passes `launched=None` and can stop the replacement. Follow `vm-unit-switch.py` Lines 4196–4230: clean up a partial boot under the original lock. After a successful boot, keep the launch identity guard for SSH or upload failures.






Also applies to: 1402-1402
findings.title: Clean up a failed boot before releasing `run.lock`.

findings.body:
**Clarify which snapshot validation remains unproven.**

This step says production snapshot validation does not exist. Lines 7–12 say `ProductionUnitAdapter.validate_snapshot` exists and that live evidence is missing. State what the production validator checks and identify the host operations that still need proof. This distinction matters when an operator evaluates a recovery record.
findings.title: Clarify which snapshot validation remains unproven.

findings.body:
**Bound total download time while holding the image lock.**

`urlopen(timeout=...)` limits blocking operations, not the whole download. A response that keeps delivering data can exceed the 1,800-second image timeout and hold `.fetch.lock` throughout, blocking other runs that use the same state directory. Enforce a monotonic transfer deadline as well as the I/O timeout. On expiry, discard the partial file without promoting it. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/urllib.request.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Bound total download time while holding the image lock.

findings.body:
**Write watchdog state atomically.**

At `apps/crq-python/ops/crq-watchdog.py`, Line 49 overwrites the live state file. If the process stops during this write, the file can contain incomplete JSON. Line 30 then raises on every later invocation, before the watchdog can send another alert. Python documents both overwrite behavior and invalid-JSON errors. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/pathlib.html?utm_source=openai))

Write a temporary file beside `ST`, then atomically replace `ST`. Apply the same change to Line 35. Handle existing malformed state explicitly so the watchdog can recover without manual file removal.
findings.title: Write watchdog state atomically.

findings.body:
**Implement the required operation output protocol.**

At `apps/crq-python/ops/crq-watchdog.py`, Lines 52-53 print narration to stdout. Lines 37 and 40 do the same. None of these paths emits a JSON result. A failed send also reaches normal process completion.

Use a shared reporter for results and errors. Emit one JSON artifact to stdout, send narration to stderr, and apply the defined exit-code mapping. Include machine-mode handling.

As per coding guidelines, I1 requires “stdout is JSON, stderr is narration; exit codes 0/1/2/3.”
findings.title: Implement the required operation output protocol.

findings.body:
**Implement the required JSON command interface.**

At `apps/crq-python/ops/fleet-reader.py:51`, a successful mirror writes narration to stdout. A caller that parses stdout as JSON fails after both snapshots have changed. `--json` also fails because the parser does not accept it.

Emit a JSON result on stdout. Send narration to stderr outside machine mode. Add `--json` handling with empty stderr and the documented JSON error artifact.

As per coding guidelines, “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout and human narration to stderr, never mixed.”
findings.title: Implement the required JSON command interface.
